chapter: Violin, the 1936 tour and the photo
title: The two-month tour and the Reserve dance hall
summary: The band toured several states for two months and nine days; the Reserve dance place drew crowds and big bands every weekend.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Where all did you travel on this tour?

I can't recall all. We played, we first played Mississippi, Arkansas, Tennessee, Alabama, Kentucky, Illinois, and Missouri. I think we made 11 and stayed in that tour. From well after we got back where we used to play around in Texas, different places. All the way. New York, Maryland, Northern City, all over.

Oh yeah? We stayed on the road two months and nine days. But every, every, you see right here there was a dancing place. People from all over, New Orleans and Hammond. All over, used to ride at reserve every Saturday night, Sunday night there and dance. And we used to play there. We played there until we got tired. Used to get, they used to get big bands to play there all the time. Did you, you knew Pierron? Pierron played the violin.
